# Saved replies (for you, the maintainer)

GitHub lets you store reusable "saved replies" under your account (Settings → Saved replies)
so you can drop a canned response into any issue or discussion in two clicks. These aren't
part of the repo — they live on your GitHub account — but here are three worth adding.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
TITLE: Please remove personal data
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Thanks for posting! It looks like this may contain real personal financial figures. Since
this space is public, please **delete this post** (not just edit it) and repost using rounded
or made-up numbers, or the built-in Example Data. Protecting your own privacy is the reason —
happy to help once it's scrubbed.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
TITLE: See the methodology (success rate)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
A lower success rate here than in other calculators is by design — the base scenario is
deliberately more pessimistic than history because the tool is built for stress-testing. This
is explained in full in METHODOLOGY.md, and trying the HISTORICAL scenario shows how much of
the gap is the model's caution versus your plan.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
TITLE: This belongs in Issues
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Thanks! This looks like a bug report rather than a discussion. Could you open it under Issues
instead? There's a short template there that captures the details I'd need to look into it.
The privacy rule is the same: no real financial data or API keys.
